author: reek
body: A watch is change DETECTION, so the only readings that mean anything are the transitions: unchanged when nothing was touched, changed when a byte moved, and unchanged AGAIN straight after -- which is the one that proves the check re-arms. Without the re-arm a single change makes a watch report as changed forever, and two watches become impossible to tell apart.

author: reek
body: The second watch is the discriminator. With one watch, a checker that reports every watch as changed and a checker that works produce the same line, so the poke touches ONLY the first region and the expected output requires the second to say `same` in the same breath.

author: reek
body: `origin-untouched` and `full-after-clear` READ A STATE THAT WAS HANDED TO A TRANSITION AND NOT TAKEN BACK. They are here because every other line in this test passes whether or not the transitions mutate their argument, and the first cut of `DevState` did mutate it: `__record-set` stores into the field and returns the same record, so a caller holding `st` found the new watch in it.

author: reek
body: The counts hid it exactly. `fill-watches s0` over a mutated `s0` starts at two and adds thirty; over a clean one it starts at zero and adds thirty-two; both answer `filled: 32`, because the cap is what that line measures. So the table-full assertion was true under both, and nothing else looked. These two lines are the only readings here that separate them -- 0 against 2, and 32 against 0.
